correctness.rationale: Reconstructed derivative isometry D:Lip_0(C_n)->H_n={g:sum g=0} in l_infinity; group averaging of any idempotent onto the 4-real-dimensional two-harmonic range preserves norm and gives the unique Fourier multiplier. The row dual norm over H_n is 1/n times minimum absolute deviations from a median c of the sampled D2 kernel, not the full-space l_infinity Lebesgue constant. For n=8 the exact 8 values have median 1/2 and sum 8+4sqrt2 giving 1+1/sqrt2; zero-sum gradient ±1 attains it. Independently integrated |D2(t)-1/2| across its four analytic zeros, obtaining exactly 10 (mean 5/pi). Reconstructed rational Machin arctan enclosures for pi and degree-30 cosine Taylor intervals with degree-32 remainder; all 15 n=5..20, n!=8 have rigorous average comparison upper <1.63 (largest certified bound approx1.62708 at n=13). For n>=21 distributional integration-by-parts of F=|D2-1/2| and Var(Fprime)<=88 proves B_n<=5/pi+44pi/(3n^2)<17/10. Independent direct median values n=5..100 confirm n=8 unique among them but only analytic plus rational certification proves all n. Uniform Riemann sums in c give limit 5/pi.
